history.p: After having finished "The Crusaders" (NWGW 172) in 1866, Gade decided to make it the last part of a trilogy on different religions. The first was to be "Kalanus", which Gade described in a letter to the Swedish composer Jacob Axel Josephson: "it is about paganism, where the longing for the true light senses a clue in a single individual".

physDesc.physMedium: Title page on a separate trimmed folio, written in blue crayon. The music written in ink with numerous cancellations and corrections in ink and pencil. Paper: 18 staves. Paginated 1-58. Last two pages unnumbered and blank. Heading on p. 1: "Kalanus" and the dating "(Pintseaften 8de Juni 1867.)". At the beginning of Part Two dated "(Mai 68)"; at the beginning of Part Three dated "(3 August 68)". After the final double bar-line on p. 58 dated "December 1868" and Gade's musical signature.
